chapter_title_en: Entering the Lion’s Den: The Imperial Capital
chapter_seo_title: Ji Ning Arrives in the Grand Xia Capital – Tracking, Treasures, and Deadly Rules
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning enters the Grand Xia imperial capital, but the Shaoyan clan immediately picks up his trail. With killing forbidden, how will they strike? Also: treasure trading at the Heavenly Treasures Mountain.
og_title: Ji Ning’s First Day in the Imperial Capital
og_description: The Shaoyan clan finds Ji Ning, but can’t act in the kill-free capital. Ji Ning heads to the Heavenly Treasures Mountain to spend his spoils—and attracts unwanted attention.
twitter_title: Ji Ning at the Capital: Under Watch
twitter_description: Ji Ning’s arrival in the Grand Xia capital is anything but quiet. The Shaoyan clan, the Heavenly Treasures Mountain’s intelligence network—everyone’s watching. Can he navigate the politics?

lore_anchors.definition: The personal conveyance of the late Shaoyan Nong, a flashy magic treasure that instantly identifies the rider as connected to the Shaoyan clan. Ji Ning uses it, making him an easy target for surveillance.
A divine sense secret art that weaponizes the cultivator’s spiritual perception into a mental shockwave. Ji Ning uses it to suppress a Primal Daoist’s probing.
The largest treasure trading hub in the Grand Xia Dynasty, headquartered in the imperial capital. It resembles a giant qilin and also operates a vast intelligence network.
The ultimate concentrated essence of natural energy, used as high-value currency among cultivators for purchasing top-grade treasures.
A social title for four wealthy, pleasure-loving scions of the Grand Xia imperial capital; denotes high status and extravagance, not peak combat power.
A rare type of magical technique that manipulates a cultivator’s spiritual perception for direct mental attacks, defenses, or manifestation, separate from Ki techniques or Fiendgod divine abilities.
